identity.notes: The app's scanner requires BOTH signals: advertised name prefix "FS" (exact, case-sensitive) AND advertised service UUID 0xFFF0. The full advertised name is unconfirmed ("FS" or e.g. "FS-XXXX") — needs a live scan. One phone can hold connections to many shoes at once; identity is per-shoe BLE address.

device.manufacturer: jtkj (app developer; shoe hardware OEM unknown)
device.name: Aurora LED Shoes
device.notes:
BLE-controlled RGB light-up shoes driven by the "Aurora LED Shoes" app (com.jtkj.auroraled, v1.0.1 analyzed). The entire protocol is a handful of 1-4 byte opcode-first packets written to a single characteristic — no header, no length, no checksum, no encryption, no handshake, no pairing, no OTA, no vendor backend (the only non-analytics HTTP in the app is a connectivity probe). Local-only viability is total.
GATT: service 0xFFF0, one characteristic 0xFFF1 used for BOTH write and notify. Writes are write-without-response (auto-split at MTU by the app's BLE wrapper). The app enables notifications ~500 ms after connect via the standard CCC descriptor 0x2902.
DEVELOPER FAMILY: jtkj also ships CoolLED1248 (com.jtkj.led1248). The two apps share the same BLE wrapper library and command-building idiom, but the GATT profile and opcodes are DIFFERENT — CoolLED1248 is the 0xFFE5/0xFFE9 family; this device is 0xFFF0/0xFFF1 with its own opcode table. Do not assume cross-compatibility; each jtkj app needs its own RE pass.
MULTI-SHOE BROADCAST: the app connects to several shoes at once and sends every command to all connected devices. A replacement client should keep one connection per shoe and broadcast writes; the shoes are independent peripherals, there is no grouping protocol.
MUSIC/MIC MODE: all signal processing is on the phone — the app runs an FFT over mic input (35 bins, picks peaks per 11-bin third, maps to RGB) and streams `01 R G B` writes live. The shoe only displays the color it is handed, so any client-side color source works.
SPEED SEMANTICS (MEDIUM confidence): the app computes the on-wire byte for `10 V` as (seekbar_max - (progress + 15)), i.e. LOWER byte value = FASTER animation (inverted slider). Persisted default is 120; a constant in the app hints the device treats speed in ~15 steps. The seekbar max lived in app resources that were not decompiled, so the exact valid on-wire range is not pinned down from code alone — treat 0-255 as the envelope and verify with a live capture.
STATE QUERY (MEDIUM confidence): writing `F0` is defined in the app as a device-state query; the device answers with a 3-byte notify frame `F0 FLAG SPEED` (FLAG 00/01 = power off/on, SPEED = current speed echo). The app only logs the response, and whether it actually sends the query in normal use is unconfirmed (possibly dead code). No handshake of any kind exists.
CONFIDENCE: service/characteristic UUIDs, discovery filter (name prefix "FS" + advertised service 0xFFF0), and all command opcodes/framing are HIGH (read directly from the app's unobfuscated command-builder code). MEDIUM: exact speed range/direction, the visual meaning of the ten `07 ...` "shining" presets, whether `F0` is live code, and the full advertised name beyond the "FS" prefix — all flagged for live capture. The shoe's BLE module is unidentified (0xFFF0/0xFFF1 is the classic cheap BLE-UART-bridge profile); no firmware/OTA capability exists.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app, and any other client holding the device, before connecting. Nothing needs clearing afterwards — no bond is stored on either side.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control — anyone nearby can change the shoes' colors.

factory_reset.effect: No credential or bond state exists on the device, so there is nothing to clear. Power-cycling the shoe drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the shoe still being connected to another phone (only one central can hold the link).

steps.action: Power the shoe off (or remove its battery) for a few seconds, then power on.
steps.expect: Shoe advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: Power the shoes on and scan for advertisements with name prefix "FS" and service 0xFFF0. Connect (no pairing/bonding), enable notifications on 0xFFF1 (the app waits ~500 ms after connect before enabling; not required for writes). Commands take effect immediately. To drive a pair, connect to both shoes and send every command to both connections.

steps.action: Power on the shoes and scan for name prefix 'FS' with service 0xFFF0.
Connect to each shoe, enable notifications on 0xFFF1 (CCC 0x2902).
Write commands to 0xFFF1 (write-without-response); broadcast to all connected shoes.

setup.notes: No provisioning. The shoe advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central — no account, no pairing PIN, no credential exchange. Scan, connect, enable notify on 0xFFF1, write.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the shoe to a phone or account — switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. Make sure the old phone's app (or OS Bluetooth auto-reconnect) is not holding the link; the app caches previously-connected MACs and reconnects to them automatically.

helpful_urls.description: The Android BLE library the app's BLE layer is built on; explains the write-without-response + auto-split-at-MTU write behavior and the CCC notify-enable flow seen in this profile.
helpful_urls.title: FastBle (open-source BLE wrapper used by the vendor app)

helpful_urls.description: Same developer, same BLE wrapper, but a DIFFERENT GATT profile (0xFFE5/0xFFE9) and opcode set. Not interchangeable with this device.
helpful_urls.title: CoolLED1248 (sibling jtkj app — different profile)

helpful_urls.title: LED shoes user manual

mode_flash.description: Flash (strobe) mode. color_id: 00 blue, 01 green, 02 red, 03 cyan, 04 purple, 05 yellow, 06 white, 10 seven-color.

mode_slow_color_change.description: Slow color-change mode. color_id selects the color(s) cycled: 00 blue, 01 green, 02 red, 03 cyan, 04 purple, 05 yellow, 06 white, 20 seven-color cycle, 30 red+green, 40 red+blue, 50 green+blue.

music_color.description: Music/mic-reactive color: set the displayed RGB color live. The vendor app computes R,G,B from phone-mic FFT; the shoe just displays whatever it receives, so any client-side color source can drive this. Stream writes as colors change.

set_speed.description: Set pattern/animation speed. LOWER byte value = FASTER (inverted slider in the app: on-wire = seekbar_max - (progress + 15)). App default is 120; device appears to treat speed in ~15 steps. Exact valid range unconfirmed — MEDIUM confidence, verify with live capture.

shining_preset.description: One of ten fixed "shining" effect presets exposed by the app. preset_id selects the exact byte string (see table below). The visual effect of each preset is UNKNOWN (MEDIUM confidence) — map by sending each and observing the shoe.

b1.notes: Preset bytes (b1 b2 [b3]; b0=0x07 always, b3 omitted for the 3-byte presets — send only the listed bytes): 06 01 00 · 01 08 · 01 13 · 03 01 00 · 09 00 · 09 01 · 0A 01 · 0A 02 · 01 01 · 02 00.

state_query.description: Query device state. Device replies on notify with the 3-byte frame `F0 FLAG SPEED` (FLAG 00/01 = power off/on, SPEED = current speed byte). MEDIUM confidence: defined in the app but only logged, never acted on — possibly dead code; confirm the reply on live hardware.

characteristics.name: Control
characteristics.notes: Single characteristic for both directions. Commands are raw opcode-first packets of 1-4 bytes, one GATT write per command — no header, length, checksum or encryption. Writes are write-without-response. Notifications carry the 3-byte state frame `F0 FLAG SPEED` in reply to the state_query command (FLAG 00/01 = power off/on, SPEED = current speed byte). Confidence: HIGH for all opcodes except where noted (speed range and the shining-preset visuals are MEDIUM, pending live capture).
